title: APU vs Gordon: tuition, size, location
summary: Azusa Pacific University (APU) versus Gordon College (Gordon). Also searched as Gordon vs APU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Gordon College vs Azusa Pacific University (Gordon vs APU) reveals differences in enrollment, tuition, and location despite both being private nonprofit institutions. Gordon College, located in Wenham, has an undergraduate enrollment of 1,278 students, whereas Azusa Pacific University in Azusa enrolls 2,759 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at Gordon is $30,700, significantly lower than Azusa Pacific's $44,458. These distinctions highlight variations in size, cost, and setting between the two schools.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost comparison between Gordon College and Azusa Pacific University (Gordon vs APU) shows notable differences in tuition fees and student debt. Both institutions charge the same tuition for in-state and out-of-state students, with Gordon College's tuition set at $30,700 and Azusa Pacific University's tuition at $44,458. This indicates that Gordon College offers a more affordable tuition rate compared to Azusa Pacific University. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who completed their programs at Gordon College is $26,250, while Azusa Pacific University graduates have a slightly lower median debt of $23,219. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments students may expect when attending either institution.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: The learning model and campus environments of Gordon College and Azusa Pacific University (Gordon vs APU) differ notably in scale and location. Gordon College, situated in Wenham, Massachusetts, serves an undergraduate population of 1,278 students, offering a smaller campus community. In contrast, Azusa Pacific University, located in Azusa, California, has a larger undergraduate enrollment of 2,759 students, reflecting a more extensive campus setting. These differences in enrollment size and geographic location contribute to distinct educational experiences at each institution.
